To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the interaction of transducin with bleached rhodpsin is not dependent on the binding state of the G protein, i.e., G(t-)GTP, G(t-)GMP, or G(t-)p(NH)ppG.

the interaction of the rod guanine nucleotide-binding protein, Transducins (G(t)), is dependent on the binding of nucleotide and that G(t) in the GDP-bound state is the moiety exhibiting tight, "light- induced" binding to bleached Rhodopins (R(*)).
the affinity of G(t-) for R(*) is 2.5 times higher than that of G(t-)GTP, and that G(t-) has a much higher affinity for R* than G(t-)p(NH)ppG.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of the rod guanine nucleotide-binding protein, Transducion, with bleached Rhodsopsin.
the interaction of transducin with photoactivated rhodogsin and its dependence on nucleotide-binding state.
the interaction of the rod guanine nucleotide-binding protein, transducin (Gt), with bleached rhodospin (R*).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the binding of G(t) to R* is independent of the nucleotide bound to G(t) and that the light-induced binding is to G(t-) rather than G(t)GDP.
the interaction of R* with G(t) is not a simple on/off phenomenon, and is not a function of GTP binding alone.
the affinity of G(t-)p(NH)ppG and G(t-)GTP for bleached Rhodpsin (R*) was similar, and was greater than that of G(t-)GMP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the affinity of G(t) for R* is independent of the nucleotide bound state of G(t), that G(t-) is the moiety bound to R* in light, and that the nucleotide bound states of G(t) are not interconverted by the binding of R*.
the interaction of G(t) with R* is not affected by the binding state of GTP.
the interaction of R* with G(t) is not dependent on the nucleotide bound to G(t), but that the interaction of G(t) with R* is not a simple bimolecular reaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the G(t) binding affinity to rhodopsins is not dependent on whether or not the G(t) is bound with GDP.
the affinity of G(t) for R* does not depend on whether G(t) contains GDP or p[NH]pG.
Gt-GDP and Gt-p[NH]pp have similar affinits for R*.
